{
 "question_intent": "Discuss the bank's dividend policy and net interest income (NII) guidance, including the impact of NIM pressure and interest rate normalization in Asia.",
 "main_topics": ["dividend policy", "net interest income", "NIM pressure", "interest rate normalization"],

 "question_quote": "I was going to also focus a little bit onto the NII guidance and whether the fact that you're not specifically talking about NIM is indicative that you are expecting now more NIM pressure and it sounds like you are, but again, I wonder if you could talk to that relating to signs of maybe slower growth in Asia.",
 "answer_quote": "I don't think we're going to see in aggregate much NIM pressure from here. Equally, I'm loath to call the bottoming out of NIM and you know I hate forecasting it for you, but I do think the combination of any relevant NIM pressure from here coupled with stronger loan growth means that we are close to getting back into a cycle now of seeing net interest income grow - and I think certainly by the time we get into 2022 we'll definitely see net interest income grow, given NIM will definitely have I think stabilised by then.",

data.question_intent: Discuss the bank's dividend policy and net interest income (NII) guidance, including the impact of NIM pressure and interest rate normalization in Asia.
data.question_quote: I was going to also focus a little bit onto the NII guidance and whether the fact that you're not specifically talking about NIM is indicative that you are expecting now more NIM pressure and it sounds like you are, but again, I wonder if you could talk to that relating to signs of maybe slower growth in Asia.
data.answer_quote: I don't think we're going to see in aggregate much NIM pressure from here. Equally, I'm loath to call the bottoming out of NIM and you know I hate forecasting it for you, but I do think the combination of any relevant NIM pressure from here coupled with stronger loan growth means that we are close to getting back into a cycle now of seeing net interest income grow - and I think certainly by the time we get into 2022 we'll definitely see net interest income grow, given NIM will definitely have I think stabilised by then.
data.reason: The answer directly addresses the question's intent, providing a clear stance on NIM pressure and interest rate normalization, with high evidence level including specific figures and forward guidance.
